## In one sentence

Supervised learning estimates a relationship between inputs and known outcomes
to predict outcomes for new inputs.

## Regression and classification

Regression predicts a numeric outcome. Classification predicts a category or
probability. Common models include linear regression, logistic regression,
trees, nearest neighbours, and neural networks.

Model choice should follow the data, target, sample size, interpretability needs,
and deployment constraints. A more flexible model can reduce training error but
may increase sensitivity to noise.

## Features and preprocessing

Encode categorical variables, handle missingness, and scale features when the
algorithm needs it. Learn preprocessing steps from training data only, then
apply the frozen steps to validation, test, and production data.

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep a simple baseline. It tells you whether model complexity produces a useful
improvement rather than merely an impressive training score.
:::

## Check your understanding

Choose a regression or classification framing for three example questions and
identify the target, features, and a suitable baseline.
